understanding: Add instruction pointers so that agents building a screen, reviewing a diff or writing a test plan run `100x plan_feature cases`: ui-baseline rule 12, diff-review rule 8b, feature-planning rule 1c, qa-strategy rule 2b, one row each in qa-engineer, code-reviewer and frontend-engineer, and the pr-review Scenario lens; examples use the generic name "Settings" and note that a project's own screen_patterns.json adds names. The CLI comes from T1, so no `cases` command in these files has been run; the AC-10 bench owes the check that agents call it.

assumptions.text: The cases, new --screens/--roles and testplan new behaviour described matches contract.md as T1 implements it; not run against the CLI (inferred).
feature-planning's coverage note (28 kinds, 202 cases) assumes T1 merges edge_cases_ui.json into plan_feature's catalogue.
The example names "Settings" and "Delete" resolve: both are names in scripts/data/screen_patterns.json.

plan_issues.issue: `cases` is a read-only lister and does not exit non-zero on a missed row.
plan_issues.impact: Naming it as the enforcer slightly overstates mechanical coverage.
plan_issues.proposal: Each tag names cases as what prints the checklist and plan_feature audit as the exit-1 gate once rows are seeded.

decisions.decision: diff-review rule placed as 8b under Both modes
decisions.basis: A missed screen row matters when reviewing your own diff too.

decisions.decision: Lettered ids 1c, 2b and code-reviewer row 2b instead of renumbering
The project-taxonomy clause sits only in ui-baseline rule 12 and feature-planning rule 1c
decisions.basis: Those are the two places that explain what a screen name is.
